newsitem.title: FRANCE: Poverty, ill-treatment of children up in France.
newsitem.headline: Poverty, ill-treatment of children up in France.

text.p: Ill-treatment of children and poverty are on the rise in France, according to surveys published on Tuesday.
A survey by the National Observatory for Decentralised Social Action (ODAS) said cases of sexual abuse of children had risen 22 percent in 1995 to 5,500 from 4,500 in 1994.
It said the total number of children battered, sexually abused or suffering serious neglect rose to 20,000 last year from 17,000 in 1994.
Another 45,000 children were classified as "in danger" because their health, security, morality or education were not safeguarded.
In a separate survey, Le Secours Catholique (Roman Catholic Relief), one of the country's largest charities said the number of people needing its aid rose by more than three per cent last year.
It was the fourth consecutive rise. France has been facing worsening unemployment for the past few years.
In a survey of 1.7 million people it helped, the charity said the proportion of young people had risen sharply: 15 percent were under 25 and a total 61 percent were under 40.
All but 17 percent were French, and most of the foreigners were from North Africa. The percentage of foreigners rose sharply in heavily-populated areas to reach 37 percent in the Paris region.
Three quarters of the needy requesting aid were unemployed, and the same proportion were urban dwellers. A quarter had no fixed address.
